name: Oral surgeon

A.flow: A: the customer comes to the business (video or phone count as A)

services.name: New patient consult with X-rays and a scan
services.story: The main story: a $35 new patient consult with X-rays and a scan. Nothing is taken. The desk checks Alex's plan, and Alex pays the share at the front desk.

services.name: New patient consult with X-rays and a scan
services.story: The same consult where the office turns on its $20 missed-visit fee. A card is saved for it, never for a fee-free patient.

services.name: Tooth removal (local numbing)
services.story: A tooth removal with local numbing, $140: a $40 deposit when booked, and the $100 rest paid at the chair after the removal.

services.name: Stitch removal and check
services.story: A $55 stitch removal and check, paid in full when booked. Nothing more is owed after.

services.name: Night guard, quoted from photos
services.story: A night guard quoted from Alex's photos at $90. A $20 deposit once the quote is OK'd, and the $70 rest at the fitting.

services.name: Post-surgery problem
services.story: A sore spot after a removal the same day. Only the $25 check is promised; any treatment is priced first, with Alex's yes.

B.flow: B: the business goes to the customer
B.staff: Jonah (oral surgeon) and Lucy (surgical assistant), who travel with a portable kit
B.customer: Alex M. (patient, lives at Riverside care home) · other patients

services.name: Check and dressing change at a care home
services.story: The main story: a $179 check and dressing change at Riverside care home. Nothing is taken. The office bills Alex's plan its own way.

services.name: Check and dressing change at a care home
services.story: The same check, paid privately: nothing is taken when booking, and Rosie texts the bill when Jonah texts DONE.

services.name: Broken tooth or loose stitch at a care home
services.story: A broken tooth or a loose stitch at the care home. Only the $89 visit fee is promised; the repair is priced at the visit, with Alex's yes first.

services.name: Multi-tooth extraction plan
services.story: A multi-tooth extraction plan, quoted by Jonah from the care-home photos and X-rays at $640. A $160 deposit once the plan is OK'd, and Rosie texts the bill for the $480 rest.

services_shape: visit types in a surgical chair, each with a set length; a tooth removal is a surgery visit with a set length and a recovery check after it; a post-surgery problem is booked the same day with the owner's OK; every visit needs a free chair
questions_before_times: for you, your child, or someone you help (a care home resident)
which visit: the office's own visit types only (a new patient consult, a tooth removal, a stitch check, a night guard, or a post-surgery problem), never a symptom typed into the AI
a dental or medical plan (its name only) or paying yourself
safety_stop: face or jaw swelling with a fever, or trouble breathing or swallowing
bleeding after a tooth removal that won't stop, or a tooth knocked out
swallowed something poisonous, or too much of a medicine
first_steps: Health history, consent and the plan's papers
A written price estimate for self-pay patients
license: each oral surgeon holds their own license from the state's dental board; a surgical assistant holds one only where the state licenses assistants
staff_skills: oral surgeons: extractions, surgical consults, night guards and post-surgery care; surgical assistants: X-rays, scans, chair setup, recovery checks and the work the state allows; only people cleared for mobile visits go to care homes and homes
messages_never: texts carry only the practice's name, the date, the time, the address and a secure link: never the visit type, the plan, the reason, the results, the medicines or the surgeon's name (when the surgeon comes to a care home or home, the name stays, for the door check); X-rays and scans never go through Rosie
demo_note: Demo data for testing only. [G] = prefilled from the business's Google listing at sign-up; the owner checks each field.
